findings.cross_file_justification: The head loader (endpoint_policy.py `_local_labels`, `_local_label_refusal`, `hop_is_local`) explicitly admits `dispatch_group: local` on the PROVIDER BLOCK and treats it as the model's locality when the entry is silent (`entry.get('dispatch_group') or prov.get('dispatch_group')`); the planner (`hop-locality.py` classify) does the same. But cheval.py populates `ModelConfig.dispatch_group` only from `model_data.get('dispatch_group')`, `openai_adapter._transport_policy` (line 221) reads only `model_config.dispatch_group`, and `modelinv.hop_locality_of` (line 476) reads only the model entry.
findings.description: A provider whose block carries `dispatch_group: local` on a loopback/RFC1918 https endpoint (no `allow_insecure_endpoint`, non-keyless so the per-model `dispatch_group` precondition does not apply) passes `validate_providers`, is classified `local` by the planner and admitted under `hounfour.locality: local_voices`, yet reaches the adapter with `model_config.dispatch_group is None` and `config.allow_insecure_endpoint is None`. `_transport_policy` returns None, so the hop is sent WITHOUT the D-7.2 request-time rules: `HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` are honoured (prompt leaves the host via the proxy), urllib follows 3xx redirects, and no path-prefix check runs. The same hop is then recorded in MODELINV with `hop_locality: hosted`, contradicting the planner's decision that admitted it.
findings.failure_mode: A hop the system planned and audited as local runs with proxy env vars honoured and redirects followed; MODELINV says `hosted` for a hop dispatched under `local_voices`, so the audit chain misstates where the prompt went.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve locality once with the loader's rule: in `_build_provider_config` set `dispatch_group=model_data.get('dispatch_group') or prov.get('dispatch_group')` (or better, compute `ModelConfig.dispatch_group='local'` iff `endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(config, provider_name, model_id)`), and make `modelinv.hop_locality_of` call `hop_is_local` instead of reading the entry label. Alternatively refuse provider-block `dispatch_group` at load so the label can only live on model entries.

findings.description: `**_modelinv_hop_telemetry(_preflight_head.canonical, hounfour)` is evaluated inside the `try:` that wraps the exit-7 (models-not-planned) MODELINV emit. `hop_telemetry` is documented fail-soft, but the attribute access on `_preflight_head` happens before it is called. If `_preflight_head` can be None at that site (the preflight could not resolve a head, which is one of the ways a call ends in exit 7), the AttributeError is swallowed by `except Exception as _emit_err` and the whole exit-7 audit row is lost, where before this change it was emitted.
findings.failure_mode: Exit-7 refusals stop producing a MODELINV row (only a stderr note), silently degrading the audit chain for the exact failures it exists to record.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `getattr(_preflight_head, 'canonical', None)` (hop_telemetry already handles None) so a missing head degrades to a row without `destination` rather than no row.

findings.description: The success-path emit derives destination/locality from `_modelinv_state['final_model_id']`. `hop_telemetry` requires a `provider:model_id` string and splits on the first `:`. If `final_model_id` holds the provider-reported model (e.g. `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, or an Ollama/llama.cpp id like `llama3.1:8b`), the first form yields no `destination`/`hop_locality` at all (silently, by design of the fail-soft), and the second is mis-split into provider `llama3.1`, model `8b`; `destination_for` then finds no provider, sees no endpoint, and records `{host: cli-subprocess, scheme: cli, provider: llama3.1}` for an HTTP local hop. The exit-7 site uses `_preflight_head.canonical` (a canonical hop), suggesting the canonical hop string, not the answering model id, is the intended input.
findings.failure_mode: Successful rows either lack the FR-8 destination/locality fields the PR claims every row carries, or record a fabricated CLI destination for a local HTTP hop.
findings.suggested_fix: Feed `hop_telemetry` the canonical `provider:model_id` of the hop that answered (the walked `_entry_target`), stored separately in `_modelinv_state`, rather than `final_model_id`; fall back to `models_failed[-1].model` / `models_requested[0]` only when no hop was reached.

findings.description: `destination_for` returns the CLI sentinel (`host: cli-subprocess, scheme: cli`) whenever `not endpoint`, which includes the case where the provider is not present in `hounfour.providers` at all (`prov == {}`) or an HTTP provider whose endpoint failed to interpolate. An unknown or misconfigured provider is thereby recorded in the audit chain as a local CLI subprocess, which is a positive claim about where the prompt went that nothing verified.
findings.failure_mode: Audit rows assert `scheme: cli` for hops that were not CLI hops, masking a misconfiguration behind a plausible-looking destination.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the CLI sentinel only when `ptype.endswith('-headless') or entry.get('kind') == 'cli'`; for an unknown provider or missing endpoint return `{host: 'unknown', scheme: 'unknown'}` (the same value already used for an unparseable endpoint).

findings.description: For policy hops the httpx client is built with `trust_env=False`. In httpx that disables not only proxy env vars (the intent) but also `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR`. The head loader deliberately admits an `https` endpoint on a loopback/RFC1918 host with `dispatch_group: local` and no opt-in; such a server almost always presents a private-CA certificate that operators trust via `SSL_CERT_FILE`. Those hops now fail TLS verification under httpx, while the urllib fallback (OpenSSL reads `SSL_CERT_FILE` natively) succeeds, so behaviour differs by which HTTP client is installed. Same pattern at the `http_get` (~397) and `http_post_stream` (~533) sites.
findings.failure_mode: A valid https local hop that worked before the policy fails with a certificate error on hosts with httpx installed, and passes on hosts without it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `trust_env=False` but pass an explicit `verify=ssl.create_default_context()` (which loads `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` via OpenSSL defaults) or construct the client with `proxies=None`/`mounts` disabled instead of `trust_env=False`, so only proxy discovery is suppressed.

findings.cross_file_justification: `pricing_source` is a ledger wire value consumed outside this diff: `cost-report.sh` (referenced in this very file as the reader of `long_context` rows) and any budget/rollup logic that tests `pricing_source == "config"`. Only `rollup.py` was updated in the diff; the truncated file list does not include `cost-report.sh`.
findings.description: Rows that previously carried `pricing_source: config` now carry `stale_catalog` for any catalog entry older than 90 days. `rollup.py` was taught the new value, but other readers of the ledger that whitelist `config`/`cli_reported` (cost-report.sh's unpriced/priced split, any dashboards or bats fixtures) will classify these priced rows as unpriced the day a catalog entry crosses the threshold, with no code change on their side. Because the threshold is wall-clock relative, this flips silently in production.
findings.failure_mode: Cost reports start under-counting priced spend and over-counting 'unpriced calls' exactly 90 days after a price_date, with no deploy to correlate it to.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep every ledger reader for `pricing_source` and add `stale_catalog` to each allow-list in the same PR (cost-report.sh at minimum), or keep `pricing_source: config` and record staleness in a separate additive field (`pricing_stale: true`) so existing consumers are unaffected.

findings.description: The schema-rejection heuristic fires on any HTTP 400 whose JSON body contains the substring `response_format` or `json_schema` anywhere. That matches the intended case (server lacks structured-output support) but equally matches (a) a hosted OpenAI 400 saying the operator's own schema is invalid (`Invalid schema for response_format ...`), and (b) a 400 that echoes the prompt back when the prompt itself mentions `json_schema`. In both cases the adapter drops the schema and re-sends the full prompt once, returning an unenforced answer with only a WARNING log. The retry also doubles the hop's wall-clock inside the same per-hop `timeout_seconds`, so a schema-bearing advisory voice near the 60s bound can now time out where it previously returned a clean 400.
findings.failure_mode: An operator's broken schema is masked as 'server rejected structured output', the voice answers unenforced, and the repair loop runs against output that was never meant to be freeform; latency for the hop doubles.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten the match to the error's `param`/`code` fields (`err.error.param in ('response_format', 'text.format')`) or to messages that say the parameter is unsupported/unknown, not merely present; and do not retry when the message indicates the schema itself is invalid.
